paradox.title: The Natural Pulse vs. The Destructive Deluge
paradox.p1: Tonle Sap is Southeast Asia’s largest freshwater lake and the biological heart of Cambodia, providing over 70% of the country’s inland protein. Every monsoon season, the Mekong River forces the Tonle Sap River to reverse its flow backward into the lake, expanding its surface area from 2,500 km² to over 16,000 km².
paradox.p2: This seasonal flood pulse is not a natural disaster — it is an ecological necessity for breeding fish and fertile sediment. However, when typhoon squalls, upstream dam discharges, and catchment saturation coincide, the lake surpasses critical emergency thresholds, submerging floating schools, drowning rice granaries, and stranding tens of thousands of households.
paradox.beneficialDesc: Predictable water rise supporting inundated forest nurseries, sediment replenishment, and sustainable floating commune migrations.
paradox.hazardDesc: Anomalous velocities > 1.8 m/s, sudden backwater surges, and bank-breaching stage heights exceeding safe village mooring thresholds.
paradox.surfaceNote: Surface expands from 2,500 km² to 16,000 km², requiring intelligent spatial discrimination of harmless inundation versus vulnerable settlement risk.

features.title: Engineered for Real-World Flood Risk Mitigation
features.subtitle: A synthesis of European Space Agency satellite constellations, European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts (ECMWF), and local ground truth telemetry.
features.f1Desc: Real-time monitoring of the Mekong–Tonle Sap reverse flow mechanism, lake stage heights, and GloFAS discharge forecasts.
features.f2Desc: Sub-catchment precipitation forecast, convective storm cell tracking, and soil saturation indices across Cambodia.
features.f3Desc: Cloud-penetrating Sentinel-1 C-band SAR radar imagery for automated inundation mapping during heavy tropical overcast.
features.f4Desc: Machine learning calibrated model distinguishing beneficial seasonal flood pulse from life-threatening catastrophic inundation.
features.f5Desc: Localized vulnerability profiles for floating villages, high-ground evacuation shelters, and commune disaster committees.
features.f6Desc: Unified ingestion pipeline linking EC JRC 38-year water occurrence, Open Development Cambodia, and FABDEM bare-earth models.
